title: Per-tenant quota lease preemption and orphaned-window reclamation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's current quota reset and lease model for reserved capacity uses fixed epoch windows and short-lived leases to coordinate token buckets across colocated services (quota service, billing reconciler, and edge rate limiters). In high churn scenarios (tenant migration, host failover, or reconciler restart) we've observed orphaned window fragments and long-lived stale leases that cause customers to temporarily exceed their reserved allocation or to be throttled incorrectly.

Problem statement:
- Stale leases can block capacity being returned to the pool for hours, leading to artificial out-of-capacity errors for other tenants.
- Preemption of active leases isn't safe today because it risks double-counting usage or losing in-flight tokens.
- Current reconciliation (periodic backfills) is slow and causes noisy billing corrections and support tickets.

Goals:
1) Provide a safe preemption mechanism for short-lived leases so we can reclaim capacity promptly during host failover or rebalancing.
2) Implement an orphaned-window reclamation flow to heal fragmented epoch windows without disturbing accurate usage accounting.
3) Minimize billing corrections and customer-impact surface area during reconciliation and rollout.

Proposed design (high level):
- Lease preemption with two-phase handshake:
  1) Preemptor marks lease as "preempting" in centralized lease metadata with preemptor-id and preempt-expiry timestamp (short TTL, e.g., 30s).
  2) Owner service attempts a graceful lease release: flush local in-flight usage to the reconciler, write commit marker to lease metadata. If successful, the lease is released immediately.
  3) If owner fails to commit by preempt-expiry, preemptor performs a guarded reclaim: it reads last-known usage marker and applies delta-based accounting to avoid double-counts, then marks the lease as transferred.
- Orphaned-window reclamation:
  - Maintain per-epoch fragment index for reserved pools (lightweight timeline entries). When fragments are older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 2x epoch length) and not associated with an active lease, a background healer aggregates fragments, computes safe deltas against billing snapshots, and collapses them into the canonical epoch entry.
- Accounting safety nets:
  - All operations are append-only and produce an immutable audit token that reconciler uses to verify idempotency.
  - Healing operations run against a snapshot and emit corrective ledger entries only when deltas are within tolerance thresholds. Large deltas require human review and are flagged to billing.

Data and migration plan:
- Phase 0 (read-only observability): add metrics and traces for lease age distribution, orphan fragment count, and reclaim attempts. No behavior changes.
- Phase 1 (opt-in reclaim): implement preemption path guarded by a tenant-level feature flag. Run reclaim on a small percentage of tenants with heavy churn. Monitor for incorrect corrections.
- Phase 2 (auto healing): enable orphaned-window healer for reserved pools with continuous monitoring and automatic rollback via feature flag if corrective ledger volume spikes.
- Phase 3 (rollout): flip default for reserved-capacity tenants and add dashboard surface in Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reclaim path returns capacity to pool within target SLO (95th percentile <= 45s) for preemption cases in controlled experiments.
- No more than 0.05% of reclaimed operations produce non-idempotent corrections requiring manual billing adjustments in the opt-in cohort.
- Orphan fragment count reduced by >90% after healer runs for 24h in test clusters.
- All reclaim/heal operations produce clear audit entries visible in the reconciler UI and Console logs.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for two-phase handshake state transitions and idempotency markers.
- Integration tests simulating owner crash during lease commit with faked last-known usage markers.
- Chaos tests with host restarts and network partitions to validate timed preemption TTL behavior.
- End-to-end simulation against the reconciliation pipeline with synthetic tenant load to validate no double-counting.

Monitoring and rollback:
- New metrics: lease_preempt_attempts, lease_preempt_success, lease_reclaim_failures, orphan_fragment_count, healer_corrective_ledger_volume.
- Dashboards: per-tenant reclaim latency, per-cluster orphan fragment map, corrective ledger volume by operation.
- Rollback strategy: revert feature flag, run compensating reconciler job to rehydrate previous state from audit ledger.

Notes and trade-offs:
- Choosing a short preempt TTL reduces stuck capacity but increases risk of reclaiming truly active owners under extreme GC pauses. We mitigate by conservative default TTL and allowing per-tenant override.
- Appendix: we considered optimistic lease expiration (no preempt handshake) but rejected it because of higher double-count risk.

Related tickets and context: this overlaps with cross-epoch reconciliation work and reserved-pool checkpointing (see ENG-20389 and ENG-51420).
comments: 2026-03-02 Asha Patel: Initial write-up and proposed handshake flow. Posting for early review from Billing and Runtime teams.
2026-03-03 Jordan Li: Runtime concerns noted — need to include KV-cache flush ordering to ensure in-flight token accounting before lease release. Added to design section.
2026-03-04 Priya Shah (Billing): Suggested delta tolerance thresholds and flagged that any corrective ledger > $1000 should open a billing incident for manual review.
2026-03-05 Miguel Torres: Implementing Phase 0 observability. Added metrics to quota-service instrumented via Prometheus. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-service/pull/412 (WIP)

2026-03-08 Chris O'Neill (SRE): Ran replay tests on staging cluster; preempt TTL 30s caused a few timed preempts during GC spikes — recommend adding per-host backoff jitter. Filing follow-up ENG-56021 for jitter paramization.
2026-03-10 Miguel Torres: Integration test harness ready. Verified idempotency marker semantics in local runs. Pushing opt-in flag rollout to 5% of tenants next week.
2026-03-12 Priya Shah (Billing): Confirmed ledger export format for corrective entries matches downstream billing importer. No schema changes required.
